consensus_summary: No fixed classical symbol; primarily a temporal figure for the brevity/transience of earthly affliction, life, or divine wrath versus eternity, plus the suddenness of eschatological change or judgment (esp. 1 Cor 15:52).
book_summary: The instant of decisive action (judgment and mercy alike), imaged by the eye’s wink, the indivisible unit in which such acts occur and never a slow process (Babylon’s fall, sudden death, resurrection).
consensus_core_identification: brevity of temporal things (esp. affliction/wrath) vs eternity, and/or suddenness of divine/eschatological action
book_core_identification: instant of decisive divine action (judgment or mercy), instantaneous like a wink, never gradual
boundary_disagreement: Book restricts the term to the unit of instantaneous decisive action covering both judgment and mercy; consensus admits broader non-action uses of pure duration/transience and elevates the affliction-vs-glory contrast as primary or co-primary.
material_contradiction: None; book selects and unifies recognized sudden-action cases without denying other contextual senses.
rationale: Both cores center on instantaneous divine timing (1 Cor 15:52 and sudden-judgment texts appear in consensus alternatives). The book preserves that general referent of suddenness but materially narrows it to ‘the instant of decisive action’ for judgment and mercy alike, built on the wink image and excluding the dominant consensus pastoral contrast of momentary affliction with eternal glory. This is boundary refinement, not core replacement or novelty.
strongest_objection: Consensus explicitly denies any settled fixed symbolic meaning and treats the momentary-affliction/eternal-glory contrast (2 Cor 4:17; Ps 30:5) as at least co-primary, an emphasis the book omits.
